patch.value: Design a deterministic execution-context contract for linked tests. Detect commands that use scripts/run-tests.mjs or self-contained benchmark fixtures; do not inject an empty schema PM_PATH when it changes their meaning, or require and persist an explicit per-test context mode with a clear add-time diagnostic. The output must show the effective context before execution and recommend the correct bounded retry. Preserve the rule that tests never read or write real repository PM data.
Linked-test schema context changes non-PM repository checks, so commands that pass directly fail when recorded and run through pm test

The 2026-08-04 audit linked existing sandbox-safe repository commands to its PM plan. The focused merge suite passed directly at 120/120, but pm test default schema context failed 1/120 because validate_merge_driver_configuration warnings appeared only under the linked sandbox. The 10k scale gate passed directly, but failed under the same inherited PM_PATH context with token and latency threshold changes. Build/typecheck and published-release verification passed in both contexts. The runner correctly isolates tracker mutations, but it silently changes semantics for non-PM commands that already create their own fixtures.

Per-test execution context is explicit, persisted, and visible before command execution.; Self-sandboxing repository test and benchmark commands have parity between direct and linked execution without access to real tracker data.; Merge and scale regression fixtures cover schema, tracker-copy, and self-sandboxing modes with guided recovery.; The runner distinguishes assertion failure caused by execution context from an actual product gate regression.
Link the focused merge suite and pnpm benchmark:scale:check to a PM item, run pm test <id> --run --progress, then run the same commands directly through scripts/run-tests.mjs and pnpm.
Sandbox-safe commands produce the same assertions and performance contract directly and through pm test, with explicit context metadata where semantic differences are intentional.
Direct merge tests pass 120/120 and direct scale gate passes; linked schema context produces merge-driver configuration warnings and scale token/latency threshold failures.
